overview.intro:
Chapter 15 covers fats and oils and the waxes made from them: olive, palm, canola, soybean, coconut, sunflower and other vegetable oils, lard, tallow and fish oil, margarine and shortening, used cooking oil and other inedible fats, crude glycerol, beeswax and carnauba wax. Its **114 tariff lines** carry a base rate on 94 of them, mostly small per-kilogram rates — 3.4¢/kg on bulk olive oil, 0.43¢/kg on tallow — with a few steep ones: **19.1% on soybean oil**, 18% on oil blends containing soybean oil, 34.2¢/kg on dairy butter substitutes over their quota. Palm oil, coconut oil and palm kernel oil are Free.

The U.S. imported **$16.03B** of these goods in 2025. Canada supplied a quarter, almost all of it canola oil, and USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico enter free. Goods from elsewhere pay the base rate **plus an extra duty by country**: since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff on 60 economies — **10% in total for EU olive oil**, +10% or +12.5% for most others, +37.5% for Brazil, up to +37.5% for China. **7 lines are exempt** for every country (coconut oil, vegetable waxes, bleached beeswax), and the country lists exempt **palm oil from Indonesia and Malaysia**. Used cooking oil and other goods of 1518.00.40 from Canada also pay a **50% Section 338 duty**. Olive oil from Tunisia, outside the 60 economies, pays only the base rate.

productGroups.label: Lard, choice white grease & other pig or poultry fat
productGroups.blurb: Rendered pig fat: lard, choice white grease and yellow grease, all at 3¢/kg. Poultry fat is here too; pig fat that is not rendered is heading 0209.

productGroups.label: Tallow & other cattle, sheep or goat fat
productGroups.blurb: Tallow and other cattle, sheep or goat fat at 0.43¢/kg, split into edible and inedible tallow. Brazil, Canada, Australia and Argentina are the main suppliers.

productGroups.label: Lard stearin, lard oil, oleo-oil & tallow oil
productGroups.blurb: Lard stearin, lard oil, oleostearin, oleo-oil and tallow oil that are not emulsified, mixed or otherwise prepared: 2¢/kg.

productGroups.label: Fish oil, cod liver oil & marine mammal oil
productGroups.blurb: Fish oils: cod liver oil and cod oil are Free; other fish-liver oil 2.5%; herring oil 1¢/kg; menhaden and other fish oil 1.5¢/kg + 5%; marine mammal oil 1.7¢/kg + 5%. Fish-oil capsules made up as supplements are classified elsewhere.

productGroups.label: Wool grease & lanolin
productGroups.blurb: Wool grease: crude at 1.3¢/kg, lanolin and other wool-grease substances 2.4%.

productGroups.label: Other animal fats & oils
productGroups.blurb: Animal fats and oils not covered elsewhere, such as neatsfoot oil or emu oil: 2.3%.

productGroups.label: Soybean oil, crude or refined
productGroups.blurb: Soybean oil carries the chapter's highest ad valorem rate: 19.1% crude or refined. Only pharmaceutical-grade oil meeting FDA requirements for intravenous fat emulsions (1507.90.20) is Free.

productGroups.label: Peanut oil
productGroups.blurb: Peanut (groundnut) oil, crude or refined: 7.5¢/kg.

productGroups.label: Olive oil: extra virgin, virgin & refined
productGroups.blurb: Olive oil by grade — extra virgin (1509.20), virgin (1509.30), other virgin (1509.40) and refined or blended (1509.90). Each pays 5¢/kg on contents and container in containers under 18 kg, or 3.4¢/kg in bulk; certified-organic oil has its own statistical lines.

productGroups.label: Olive-pomace oil & other olive oils
productGroups.blurb: Olive-pomace oil (extracted with solvents) and blends with olive oil, at the same rates as olive oil; pomace oil rendered unfit for food is Free.

productGroups.label: Palm oil & palm olein, crude or refined
productGroups.blurb: Crude palm oil (1511.10) and refined, bleached and deodorized palm oil, palm olein and palm stearin (1511.90): Free. Palm oil from Indonesia and Malaysia is on their Section 301 exception lists.

productGroups.label: Sunflower, safflower & cottonseed oil
productGroups.blurb: Sunflower-seed and safflower oil at 1.7¢/kg + 3.4%, crude or refined (organic sunflower oil has its own lines); cottonseed oil at 5.6¢/kg.

productGroups.label: Coconut oil, palm kernel oil & babassu oil
productGroups.blurb: Coconut (copra) oil, palm kernel oil and babassu oil: all Free. Coconut oil, crude or refined, is on the Section 301 exemption list for every country; palm kernel oil only on some country lists.

productGroups.label: Canola (rapeseed) & mustard oil
productGroups.blurb: Canola (low erucic acid rapeseed) oil at 6.4%, crude or refined. Rapeseed or mustard oil imported to make rubber substitutes or lubricants is Free; denatured oil 1.3¢/kg.

productGroups.label: Corn, sesame, linseed, castor, avocado, jojoba & other vegetable oils
productGroups.blurb: Every other vegetable oil: corn oil 3.4%, linseed oil 6.3¢/kg, sesame oil 0.68¢/kg, castor oil and nut oils Free, jojoba 2.3%, microbial oils and hemp, avocado, argan and other oils 3.2%.

productGroups.label: Hydrogenated & interesterified fats and oils
productGroups.blurb: Fats and oils that have been hydrogenated, interesterified or re-esterified but not further prepared: animal 7¢/kg, rapeseed 7.7%, other vegetable and microbial 8.8¢/kg.

productGroups.label: Margarine, shortening & edible oil blends
productGroups.blurb: Margarine at 12.3¢/kg; oil blends and shortenings at 18% if they contain 5% or more soybean oil, otherwise 8%; dairy butter substitutes under a tariff-rate quota (11¢/kg in quota, 34.2¢/kg over it); other edible preparations 8.8¢/kg.

productGroups.label: Chemically modified & inedible fats and oils, incl. used cooking oil
productGroups.blurb: Boiled, oxidized or otherwise chemically modified fats and oils, and inedible mixtures of fats — including used cooking oil (1518.00.40, 8%). Linseed-based products are 6.3¢/kg.

productGroups.label: Crude glycerol, glycerol waters & lyes
productGroups.blurb: Crude glycerol, glycerol waters and glycerol lyes: Free. Refined glycerol is Chapter 29.

productGroups.label: Vegetable waxes (carnauba, candelilla), beeswax & insect waxes
productGroups.blurb: Carnauba, candelilla and other vegetable waxes, and beeswax and other insect waxes: Free, except bleached beeswax at 4.8%. Vegetable waxes and bleached beeswax are on the Section 301 exemption list.

productGroups.label: Degras & residues from treating fats or waxes
productGroups.blurb: Degras and residues from treating fats, oils or waxes, such as soapstocks and oil foots: 3.8%.

workedExamples.title: A tanker of refined canola oil from Canada
workedExamples.body: The general rate is 6.4%. Canadian canola oil claimed under USMCA (SPI **S**) is Free, and USMCA-qualifying goods are exempt from the Section 301 duty (9903.05.93), so on $1,000,000 the duty is **$0**. Oil that does not qualify pays 6.4% + 10% (9903.05.29) = **$164,000**.

workedExamples.title: 10,000 kg of bottled extra virgin olive oil from Spain — or Tunisia
workedExamples.body: In containers under 18 kg the rate is 5¢/kg on contents and container, so 10,000 kg gross = $500. On $90,000 of oil that is under 1% of value, so the EU Section 301 rule (9903.05.39) lifts the total to 10%: **$9,000**. The same oil from Tunisia, which is not one of the 60 economies, pays only **$500**.

workedExamples.title: $500,000 of refined palm oil from Indonesia
workedExamples.body: Palm oil is Free, and 1511.90.00 is on Indonesia's Section 301 exception list (U.S. note 52(j), 9903.06.16), so the duty is **$0**. From Colombia, which has no exception list, it is 12.5% (9903.05.32) = **$62,500**; from China 12.5% + 7.5% = **$100,000**.

workedExamples.title: $200,000 of used cooking oil from Canada
workedExamples.body: Used cooking oil is 1518.00.40 (CBP ruling N347194), general rate 8%. Since September 15, 2026 this line carries the 50% Section 338 duty on Canadian goods (9903.03.12), which applies even when USMCA is claimed: **$100,000** with USMCA, 8% + 10% + 50% = **$136,000** without it.

seo.shortDescription: What changed for HTS Chapter 15 fats and oils since January 2025: the end of the IEEPA and Section 122 duties, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs and the palm and coconut oil exemptions, the Section 338 duty on Canadian used cooking oil and new palm oil forced-labor orders, with official citations.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). No Chapter 15 base rate changed between them; six new statistical lines split out certified-organic coconut oil and avocado oil at the same rates.

Everything that changed came on top of the base rate. The 2025 IEEPA duties (Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil and the reciprocal tariff on everyone else) **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026**, goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%** (10% in total for EU goods) — except coconut oil, vegetable waxes and bleached beeswax for every country, and palm, palm kernel, castor and some other oils on the exception lists of Indonesia, Malaysia and nine other economies. China pays its 2018–2019 Section 301 duties too, Brazil an extra 25%, and since **September 15, 2026** used cooking oil and other goods of 1518.00.40 from Canada pay **+50% under Section 338**. **USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico are exempt from the Section 301 duties.**
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 15 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their exemption and country exception lists, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, the China Section 301 Lists 3 and 4A, the Section 338 duty on Canada, the phased Nicaragua duty, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended. CBP forced-labor orders on palm oil and the biofuel rules that shape demand for imported fats are listed as reference entries. No antidumping or countervailing duty order covers a Chapter 15 line. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

changes.title: No Chapter 15 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 108 Chapter 15 lines that exist in both editions carry the same General, FTA and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition. The six new 10-digit lines split existing ones at the same rate: certified-organic and other refined coconut oil (1513.19.00.30/.90) and avocado oil, organic and other, and other oils, organic and other, under 1515.90.81.

changes.title: Nicaragua Section 301 duty: 10% from 2027, 15% from 2028
changes.detail: USTR set a phased duty on products of Nicaragua (9903.89.01): 0% in 2026, 10% from January 1, 2027 and 15% from January 1, 2028. It does not apply to goods that originate under CAFTA-DR and are entered under it (U.S. note 29). It comes on top of the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty on Nicaragua (9903.05.58).

changes.title: China Section 301 duties continued
changes.detail: After its four-year review USTR continued the 2018–2019 Section 301 actions on China. For Chapter 15, List 4A (+7.5%, 9903.88.15) covers 104 lines and List 3 (+25%, 9903.88.03) 9 lines; they stack with the 12.5% 2026 duty.

changes.title: CBP detains palm oil from two Indonesian producers
changes.detail: CBP issued Withhold Release Orders under 19 U.S.C. 1307 against palm oil and its derivative products made by Mitra Aneka Rezeki and Hardaya Inti Plantation in Indonesia. Their shipments — and products traceable to their oil — are detained at every U.S. port unless the importer proves no forced labor was used. It does not change the tariff: palm oil from other Indonesian producers is still Free.

changes.title: Section 338 duty on Canadian used cooking oil and inedible fats
changes.detail: Proclamation 11064 added 34 provisions to the 50% Section 338 duty on products of Canada (9903.03.12), from September 15, 2026. One is Chapter 15: 1518.00.40, which covers used cooking oil and other inedible or chemically modified fat mixtures. The duty applies on top of the general rate and any Section 301 duty, and also to goods entered under USMCA (U.S. note 51(a)).

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies — coconut oil, waxes and Indonesian and Malaysian palm oil exempt
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84), on 107 of 114 Chapter 15 lines. The general exemption list (U.S. note 52(b), 9903.05.86) covers 7 lines: coconut oil, vegetable waxes and bleached beeswax. Country exception lists (note 52(j)) exempt palm oil and other tropical oils for Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Ecuador, Jordan, Guatemala, El Salvador and others. EU goods pay 10% in total and Japan, South Korea and Switzerland 12.5% in total where the base rate is lower. USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94).

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on goods of Brazil (9903.05.01). Its exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03) has the same four Chapter 15 subheadings as the 2026 list — coconut oil, vegetable waxes (including carnauba) and bleached beeswax. From July 24 the 12.5% 2026 tariff (9903.05.27) is added on top, so Brazilian tallow and lard pay +37.5%.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still apply.

changes.title: EPA sets 2026–2027 biofuel volumes; import RIN cut postponed
changes.detail: EPA's final Renewable Fuel Standard rule for 2026 and 2027 raised the volume requirements but did not finalize the proposed "import RIN reduction", which would have given fewer RINs to fuel made from imported feedstocks such as canola oil, tallow or used cooking oil. EPA said it intends to adopt it from the 2028 compliance year or shortly after. No tariff change.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs — coconut oil and waxes exempt
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. The product exemption list (9903.03.03) covered the same four Chapter 15 subheadings as the reciprocal-tariff exemption: coconut oil, vegetable waxes and bleached beeswax. USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico were exempt (9903.03.07, 9903.03.08).

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: CBP lifts the detention order on FGV palm oil
changes.detail: CBP modified the September 30, 2020 Withhold Release Order on palm oil and palm oil products of FGV Holdings Berhad (Malaysia), after the company remediated forced labor. understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 15 goods fell from **$17.20B in 2024 to $16.03B in 2025** (-6.8%), after more than doubling since 2020 ($6.87B). The largest groups are canola oil (heading 1514, $3.09B), chemically modified and inedible fats (1518, $2.58B), olive oil (1509, $2.41B), palm oil (1511, $1.81B), coconut and palm kernel oil (1513, $1.80B) and tallow (1502, $1.30B).

Each big supplier has its own product. **Canada** ($4.00B, down from $5.12B) ships canola oil — $3.04B of it. **Indonesia** ($2.44B) ships palm oil ($1.49B) and coconut and palm kernel oil ($767M); **Malaysia** ($827M, +61%) mostly heading 1518 and palm oil. **Spain** ($1.19B), **Italy** ($969M) and **Tunisia** ($345M) supply olive oil, and the **Philippines** ($767M) coconut oil. Heading 1518 — which includes used cooking oil (CBP ruling N347194) — comes mainly from China ($613M), Australia ($428M), Malaysia, Canada and South Korea, and tallow mainly from Brazil ($445M), Canada and Australia. **Mexico** ($627M) ships mostly heading 1515, which includes avocado oil.

Many of these fats are feedstocks for biodiesel and renewable diesel, so U.S. biofuel rules move demand as much as tariffs do: since 2026 the section 45Z credit only counts fuel made from North American feedstock. USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico — 29% of 2025 imports — enter free, and palm and coconut oil are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty for their main suppliers. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

assumptions: Each total was computed by the official-measures calculator engine (the same data as the tariff calculator: measures.json, HTSUS 2026 Revision 21) for goods entered on 2026-10-12, priced on a $10,000 shipment and 1,000 units for per-unit rates.
Ranges like "Free · 11.8%" mean the group has lines with different base rates; select a cell to see which lines carry which rate.
A per-unit rate plus a percentage cannot be added into one number without the shipment’s weight, count or volume, so it is shown as written.
Preferences: USMCA (S) is applied for Canada and Mexico on the "USMCA-qualifying" side; AU for Australia. GSP (A, A+) has lapsed and is not applied. Other preferences are not applied.
Conditional relief is not applied (it needs the importer's confirmation): 9903.06.01 (Section 301), 9903.06.11 (Section 301), 9903.06.13 (Section 301), 9903.06.15 (Section 301).
Any other country shows the range across every country not listed (column 2 countries — Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus — aside), without preferences.
The IEEPA duties (9903.01.xx, 9903.02.xx) are still printed in the schedule but ended February 24, 2026, and the Section 122 surcharge (9903.03.01) expired July 23, 2026; neither is applied.
The 2019 Large Civil Aircraft duties (9903.89.13, olive oil from Germany, Spain and the United Kingdom) are printed but suspended since 2021 and are not applied.
The 7 lines on the Section 301 general exemption list (U.S. note 52(b)) and the lines on each matrix country's own exception list (note 52(j)) are priced with no 2026 Section 301 duty.
Antidumping and countervailing duties: no order covers a Chapter 15 line. Federal excise taxes do not apply to these goods.

Dairy butter substitutes (1517.90.45, 1517.90.50) are in-quota lines that need general note 15 or a USDA import licence; the over-quota line (1517.90.60) can also face an agricultural special safeguard duty (9904.04) that is not included.
The rate is not the only gate: CBP Withhold Release Orders detain palm oil from named producers, and animal fats must meet APHIS and FSIS entry rules (see the documents page).

seo.title: Importing Olive Oil, Palm Oil & Edible Oils: FDA, USDA & CBP Rules and Legal Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 15) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The entry rules for each HTS Chapter 15 line — FDA registration, prior notice and FSVP, APHIS and FSIS rules for tallow and lard, CBP palm-oil forced-labor orders, dairy licences — plus the legal ways to pay less: USMCA, exemption lists, bulk containers, actual-use lines, drawback.

importing palm oil forced labor wro

tariffEngineering.intro:
For fats and oils, **who made the oil and what it came from** decide whether a shipment is released. Every edible line needs a registered foreign facility, prior notice and an importer with a Foreign Supplier Verification Program. Lard and tallow must also clear APHIS and FSIS animal-product rules, and palm oil from producers under a CBP Withhold Release Order is detained however it is classified.

The ways to pay less are written into the schedule: claim **USMCA** or another FTA, check the **Section 301 exemption and country lists** (coconut oil, palm oil from Indonesia and Malaysia), ship olive oil in **bulk containers** of 18 kg or more, use the **actual-use lines** for industrial rapeseed oil, or claim **drawback**. No antidumping or countervailing duty order applies to this chapter.

levers.title: Claim USMCA on goods from Canada or Mexico
levers.saves: The Section 301 duty (10% of value) plus the base rate — 6.4% on canola oil, 19.1% on soybean oil, 8% on oil blends
levers.appliesTo: All 114 lines, for goods that qualify as originating under USMCA
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer. It need not follow a prescribed format; it can be on the invoice or another document, and CBP can ask for it.
levers.caveat: Oil crushed in Canada or Mexico from seed grown elsewhere may not qualify; check the product-specific rule. The 50% Section 338 duty on Canadian 1518.00.40 (used cooking oil) applies even to USMCA goods. The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

citations.label: USTR statement on the USMCA joint review (July 1, 2026)

levers.title: Claim another free trade agreement
levers.saves: The base rate: nearly every dutiable line is Free for FTA partners such as Australia, Chile, Colombia, Israel, Korea, Morocco, Peru and CAFTA-DR
levers.appliesTo: Dutiable lines, for originating goods of the partner country (the special-rate column lists who qualifies)
levers.document: Proof of origin as the agreement requires (certification or declaration), kept on file and given to CBP on request.
levers.caveat: An FTA claim removes the base rate but not the 2026 Section 301 duty for that country (U.S. note 52(a)). Dairy butter substitutes over quota (1517.90.60) are Free only for the partners named on the line.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Check the Section 301 exemption list
levers.saves: The whole 2026 Section 301 duty (10%–12.5%, or 25% + 12.5% for Brazil) — the line pays only its base rate
levers.appliesTo: 7 lines for every country: coconut oil, crude and refined (1513.11, 1513.19), vegetable waxes such as carnauba and candelilla (1521.10), bleached beeswax (1521.90.20)
levers.document: Correct classification on the entry (the exemption follows the HTS subheading; it is filed with 9903.05.86 / 9903.05.03).
levers.caveat: Palm kernel oil (1513.21, 1513.29) is not on the general list. China still pays its List 4A duty on these lines.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 50(a)(ii) and 52(b)

levers.title: Use the supplier country's exception list (palm and other tropical oils)
levers.saves: The 2026 Section 301 duty (10%–12.5%) on palm oil, palm kernel oil, castor oil, nut oils or jojoba oil from the listed countries
levers.appliesTo: Indonesia, Cambodia, Ecuador, Jordan: palm, palm kernel, castor, nut and jojoba oils; Malaysia: palm, refined palm kernel and castor oil; Guatemala and El Salvador: some of these; Switzerland: castor and nut oils; Argentina: jojoba; Bangladesh: castor; Taiwan: refined palm oil. Argan oil (1515.90.81) by description for Malaysia, Argentina, Bangladesh and Taiwan.
levers.document: Entry of goods that are products of the listed country, filed with that country's exception heading (9903.05.98–9903.06.21).
levers.caveat: The lists follow origin, not the shipping port: palm oil refined or transshipped elsewhere takes the origin CBP assigns. Other countries (Colombia, Brazil, the Philippines for palm kernel oil) pay the duty.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(j)

levers.title: Import olive oil in bulk and bottle it in the U.S.
levers.saves: Olive and pomace oil in containers of 18 kg or more pay 3.4¢/kg on the oil instead of 5¢/kg on contents and container
levers.document: Entry under the "Other" (bulk) subheading, with the container weight shown on the packing list.
levers.caveat: For EU, Turkish and other Section 301 origins the percentage duty (10%–12.5% of value) is far larger than either per-kg rate, so the saving is small there.

levers.title: Use the actual-use and special-grade lines
levers.saves: Free instead of 6.4% (rapeseed or mustard oil for rubber substitutes or lubricants), Free instead of 19.1% (pharmaceutical-grade soybean oil for intravenous fat emulsions), Free instead of 3.4¢–5¢/kg (pomace oil rendered unfit for food)
levers.document: For actual-use lines, proof of use within 3 years of entry kept by the importer and available to CBP; for 1507.90.20, proof the oil meets FDA requirements for intravenous use.
levers.caveat: Goods not used as declared owe the higher duty. The 2026 Section 301 duty still applies to these lines.

levers.title: Enter dairy butter substitutes within the quota
levers.saves: 11¢/kg in quota instead of 34.2¢/kg over quota
levers.appliesTo: Butter substitutes and other dairy fat blends of 1517.90 (1517.90.45, 1517.90.50 vs 1517.90.60)
levers.document: A USDA dairy import licence for licensed quota goods (additional U.S. note 10 to chapter 4), or entry under general note 15.
levers.caveat: Over-quota goods can also face an agricultural special safeguard duty (9904.04); Australia and Colombia have their own FTA quotas (9822.04.25, 9918.04.60).

levers.title: Claim drawback on goods you export or destroy
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the ordinary customs duties paid, when the imported oil (or goods made from it) is exported or destroyed
levers.appliesTo: Any line, for importers who re-export — for example oil refined or blended and shipped abroad
levers.document: A drawback claim filed with CBP with proof of import, use and export.
levers.caveat: Confirm with CBP whether a given Chapter 99 duty is eligible before relying on it.

levers.title: Get a binding ruling before you import
levers.saves: Certainty: a ruling fixes the classification — virgin vs. refined olive oil, blend vs. single oil, edible vs. inedible, 1518 vs. fatty acids of Chapter 38 — before the goods arrive
levers.appliesTo: Any line where the classification decides the rate
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP describing the product, its composition and how it is processed and packed.
levers.caveat: Rulings apply to the transaction described. Fatty acids and refined glycerol are outside Chapter 15 (Chapters 38 and 29), and fatty acids from Indonesia and Malaysia are under antidumping and countervailing duty investigation.

rules.title: Food facility registration: the foreign plant that makes, packs or holds the food must be registered with FDA
Prior notice of every food shipment before it arrives
Foreign Supplier Verification Program (FSVP): the importer must verify that each foreign supplier produces the food safely
Partially hydrogenated oils (PHOs) are not allowed in food: FDA revoked their remaining authorized uses, including in margarine and shortening, from December 22, 2023
Seafood HACCP: edible fish oils are fishery products; the importer must hold proof the foreign processor follows seafood HACCP
Edible lard and tallow are meat food products: only from countries and establishments FSIS lists as eligible, with a foreign health certificate, and reinspected at entry
Animal disease rules: tallow, processed fats and their derivatives from ruminants are restricted for BSE unless the conditions of 9 CFR 95.4 are met
Dairy import licence for butter substitutes entered under the licensed tariff-rate quota
Certified-organic lines: an NOP import certificate for each organic shipment

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about importing fats and oils into the U.S. — tariffs by country, HS codes and the rules that decide whether a shipment is released. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico enter free — no base rate, no Section 301 duty — except Canadian used cooking oil (1518.00.40), which pays 50% under Section 338.

The 2025 IEEPA tariffs ended on February 24, 2026. Since July 24, 2026 the extra duty is a Section 301 tariff: 10% in total for EU olive oil, +10% or +12.5% for most other suppliers, +37.5% for Brazil and up to +37.5% for China.
Coconut oil and vegetable waxes are exempt for every country, and palm oil is exempt for Indonesia, Malaysia and other countries with exception lists. Tunisian olive oil pays only its base rate.
No antidumping order covers these goods, but CBP forced-labor orders can stop palm oil from named producers, and animal fats must meet USDA rules.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on olive oil imported into the U.S.?
searchedAs: are there tariffs on olive oil
faqs.answer: Yes. The base rate is small — 5¢/kg on contents and container for bottles under 18 kg, 3.4¢/kg in bulk — but most suppliers also pay the 2026 Section 301 duty. EU olive oil pays 10% of value in total, Turkish olive oil the base rate plus 12.5%. Olive oil from Tunisia, which is not one of the 60 economies, pays only the base rate, and FTA partners such as Morocco or Chile pay no base rate but still pay the 12.5% Section 301 duty.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on olive oil from Spain, Italy or Greece?
searchedAs: tariff on olive oil from spain
are there tariffs on italian olive oil
tariffs on olive oil from greece
faqs.answer: 10% of value in total. Since July 24, 2026 EU goods whose base rate is under 10% pay 10% in all (9903.05.39), and olive oil's 3.4¢–5¢/kg is far below that. This replaced the 15% IEEPA rate that ended February 24, 2026. The 25% duty on Spanish olive oil from the 2019 Airbus dispute (9903.89.13) is still suspended.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for olive oil?
searchedAs: hs code for olive oil extra virgin
hs code for virgin olive oil
hs code for pomace olive oil
faqs.answer: Heading 1509: extra virgin olive oil 1509.20, virgin olive oil 1509.30, other virgin olive oils (such as lampante) 1509.40, and refined or blended ("pure") olive oil 1509.90. Olive-pomace oil is 1510. In the U.S. schedule each splits by container — under 18 kg (1509.20.20, 5¢/kg on contents and container) or bulk (1509.20.90, 3.4¢/kg) — and certified-organic oil has its own statistical suffix.

faqs.question: Is palm oil exempt from U.S. tariffs?
faqs.answer: Palm oil has no base rate (Free), and palm oil from Indonesia and Malaysia is on their Section 301 exception lists, so it pays nothing. Cambodia, Ecuador, Jordan, Guatemala, El Salvador and Taiwan (refined palm oil) have the same exemption. From Colombia, Brazil or the Philippines palm oil pays the 12.5% Section 301 duty (37.5% for Brazil), and from China 20%. Palm oil from producers under a CBP forced-labor order is detained.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for palm oil and palm kernel oil?
searchedAs: hs code for crude palm oil
hs code for refined palm oil
hs code for rbd palm oil
hs code for palm kernel oil
faqs.answer: Crude palm oil is 1511.10.00; refined, bleached and deodorized (RBD) palm oil, palm olein and palm stearin are 1511.90.00. Palm kernel oil is 1513.21.00 (crude) or 1513.29.00 (other). All are Free. Hydrogenated palm oil is 1516.20, and palm fatty acid distillate and other fatty acids are Chapter 38.

faqs.question: Which palm oil imports are blocked for forced labor?
searchedAs: rspo certified palm oil trade regulations
faqs.answer: On September 29, 2026 CBP issued Withhold Release Orders on palm oil and its derivative products made by Mitra Aneka Rezeki and Hardaya Inti Plantation in Indonesia; their shipments are detained unless the importer proves no forced labor was used. CBP lifted its order on FGV Holdings (Malaysia) on January 15, 2026 and ended its Sime Darby finding in 2023. Certification schemes are not a legal substitute for that proof.

faqs.question: Is coconut oil exempt from tariffs, and what is its HS code?
searchedAs: hs code for virgin coconut oil
faqs.answer: Yes. Coconut oil is 1513.11.00 (crude) or 1513.19.00 (other, including refined and virgin coconut oil, with a certified-organic suffix), with no base rate, and both are on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list for every country. Only China still adds its 7.5% List 4A duty. Coconut oil was also exempted from the reciprocal tariff in November 2025 and from the Section 122 surcharge.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on soybean oil?
faqs.answer: Soybean oil is 1507.10 (crude) and 1507.90.40 (once-refined or fully refined), both 19.1% — the highest ad valorem rate in the chapter. Pharmaceutical-grade oil for intravenous fat emulsions (1507.90.20) is Free. Section 301 duties come on top for most origins; USMCA-qualifying soybean oil from Canada or Mexico is Free. Blends containing 5% or more soybean oil are 1517.90.10 at 18%.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on canola oil from Canada?
faqs.answer: Canola oil is 1514.11.00 (crude) or 1514.19.00 (other), with a 6.4% base rate. USMCA-qualifying canola oil from Canada is Free and exempt from the 10% Section 301 duty; oil that does not qualify pays 16.4%. Canada shipped $3.04B of canola oil to the U.S. in 2025, the chapter's largest single flow.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and tariff for sunflower oil?
searchedAs: hs code for refined sunflower oil
hs code high oleic sunflower oil
faqs.answer: Sunflower-seed oil is 1512.11 (crude) or 1512.19 (refined and other), at 1.7¢/kg + 3.4%; high-oleic sunflower oil is classified the same way, and organic oil has its own statistical suffix. Ukrainian sunflower oil pays only that rate; Argentine oil adds 10% and Turkish oil 12.5% under Section 301.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and tariff for used cooking oil?
searchedAs: hs code for used cooking oil
faqs.answer: CBP classifies used cooking oil in 1518.00.40 (ruling N347194), with an 8% base rate. Since September 15, 2026 Canadian used cooking oil pays a 50% Section 338 duty even under USMCA. From China it pays 8% + 20%, from Malaysia 8% + 10%. Imported used cooking oil from outside North America no longer earns the 45Z clean fuel credit.

faqs.question: What is the tariff code for fish oil and cod liver oil?
searchedAs: hs code for cod liver oil
faqs.answer: Fish-liver oils are 1504.10 — cod liver oil Free, others 2.5%. Other fish oils are 1504.20: cod Free, herring 1¢/kg, menhaden and other fish oil 1.5¢/kg + 5%. Fish-oil capsules put up as dietary supplements are generally classified outside Chapter 15. From China fish oils add 37.5% in Section 301 duties.

faqs.question: What is the tariff code for avocado oil?
faqs.answer: Avocado oil is 1515.90.81 (statistical suffixes .20 certified organic, .40 other), at 3.2%. USMCA-qualifying avocado oil from Mexico is Free; from other Section 301 economies the duty is added on top.

faqs.question: What is the tariff code for margarine and shortening?
faqs.answer: Margarine (not liquid) is 1517.10.00 at 12.3¢/kg. Shortenings, frying fats and cooking-oil blends are 1517.90: 18% if they contain 5% or more soybean oil (1517.90.10), otherwise 8% (1517.90.20). Dairy-based butter substitutes are under a tariff-rate quota: 11¢/kg in quota, 34.2¢/kg over it. Partially hydrogenated oils may no longer be used in these foods.

faqs.question: What is the tariff code for beeswax?
faqs.answer: Beeswax is heading 1521.90: bleached beeswax 1521.90.20 at 4.8%, other beeswax and insect waxes 1521.90.40 Free. Carnauba and candelilla waxes are 1521.10, Free. Bleached beeswax and vegetable waxes are on the Section 301 exemption list for every country.
